metadata.annas_title: The Yacoubian Building : A Novel Alaa Al Aswany, Humphrey Davies (translation) HarperCollins e-books, Open Road Integrated Media, Inc., Pymble, NSW, 2006 A fading aristocrat & self-proclaimed ‘scientist of women.’ A purring, voluptuous siren. A young shop-girl enduring the clammy touch of her boss & hating herself for accepting the modest banknotes he tucks into her pocket afterward. An earnest, devout young doorman, feeling the irresistible pull toward fundamentalism. A cynical, secretly gay newspaper editor, helplessly in love with a peasant security guard. A roof-squatting tailor, scheming to own property. A corrupt & corpulent politician, twisting the Koran to justify taking a mistress. All live in the Yacoubian Building, a once-elegant temple of Art Deco splendor slowly decaying in the smog & hubbub of downtown Cairo, Egypt. In the course of this unforgettable novel, these disparate lives converge, careening inexorably toward an explosive conclusion. Tragicomic, passionate, shockingly frank in its sexuality, & brimming with an extraordinary, embracing human compassion, The Yacoubian Building is a literary achievement of the first order. This exceptional Egyptian novel – as mesmerising as it is controversial – caused an unprecedented stir when it was first published in Arabic. Welcome to the Yacoubian Building, Cairo: once grand, now dilapidated, & full of stories & passion. Some live in squalor on its rooftop while others inhabit the faded glory of its apartments & offices. Within these walls religious fervour jostles with promiscuity; bribery with bliss; modern life with ancient culture. At ground level, Taha, the doorman’s son, harbours career aspirations & romantic dreams – but when these are dashed by unyielding corruption, hope turns to bitterness, with devastating consequences.Inspired the highest-budget Arabic-language film ever, which was released to much acclaim in 2006. Alaa Al Aswanyis the bestselling author of three previous books published in ArabicHumphrey Davies translated Thebes at War by Naguib Mahfouz.
